court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Civil Judge Senior Division, Dhule in HMP No.314/2024
case_name: Dimpal Nikhilkumar Sanklecha vs Nikhilkumar Nandakumar Sanklecha
facts_of_case: Petitioner-wife seeks to challenge an order allowing respondent-husband's application for her medical examination by an expert psychiatrist.

legal_principles.principle: The matrimonial Court possesses sufficient powers to direct medical examination in case a decree for divorce under Section 13(1)(iii) of Hindu Marriage Act is sought.
legal_principles.held: It cannot be disputed that matrimonial Court possesses sufficient powers to direct medical examination in case decree for divorce under Section 13(1)(iii) of Hindu Marriage Act is sought.
cited_cases: Sushma w/o Umesh Kanpathak Vs. Umesh s/o Vijayrao Kanpathak, 2018(1) Mh.L.J. 51

legal_principles.principle: The burden of the petitioner lies in establishing that unsoundness of mind of respondent is incurable, or that mental condition is such as to render the respondent unfit for marriage.
legal_principles.held: In such cases, it is burden of petitioner to establish that unsoundness of mind of respondent is incurable, or that mental condition is such as to render the respondent unfit for marriage.

outcome.final_order: The writ petition is allowed, and the trial court's order directing the petitioner's medical examination is set aside.
